question: How the chat during play works: what opens and closes it, recipients, sending, showing, the lines the game writes, and whether chat.gui is used.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::CloseChatWindow
addresses.comment: **The handler of menubar.gui's `chat_window` `closebutton`** (the CButtonObserverGlue at +0x788, attached in CInGameIdler::Enter at 0x65FC55 and again by ReloadMenubar). Where message_log_open (+0x1D8A) is set, CInGameIdler::ToggleMessageLog; `chat_window`'s `chat_message` (window slot 16) gets keeps_focus (+0x41) = 0; `chat_window` hidden (CGuiObject slot 14); the combat view (+0x1364), where there is one, gets its window's slot 24. **Nothing in the image shows this window, so the handler is never reached** - see reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ingamechat.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0x64CBA0..0x64CCDA (bare ret). No direct caller (findRefs --callers: 0); one code reference, `mov eax, 0x64cba0` at 0x647A3D in CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler, stored into the glue at +0x788. Wrong if a call of slot 13 on `chat_window` exists that the 24-reference census of the name missed.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::ToggleMessageLog
addresses.comment: The handler of `messagelog_window`'s `closebutton` and of the menubar's `OPENbutton` (the glue at +0xA30; both attached in Enter, 0x65FB7B and 0x66006E). Nothing where the latch +0xA80 is set; otherwise, by whether `messagelog_window` is shown (+0x5B): shown - the window hidden, `OPENbutton` shown, message_log_open (+0x1D8A) = 0; hidden - message_log_open = 1, the window shown, `OPENbutton` hidden; either way the combat view (+0x1364) is told (its window's slot 24 with the log's size) and +0xA80 = 1. Also called by Enter (0x6602E7) and by CInGameIdler::CloseChatWindow. Read for the chat; the latch's clearer was not looked for.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0x64C8C0..0x64CB91 (bare ret). Callers 0x64B3CA, 0x64B62A, 0x64CBC9, 0x6602E7; the constructor stores it into the glue at +0xA30 (0x647B84). Wrong if +0x5B is not the window's shown byte (window slot 8 writes 1 there, slot 9 writes 0: VA 0xAC2650, 0xAC2230).

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::OnChatAlliesButton
addresses.comment: **`chat_window`'s `allies` button** (glue +0x828). Walks the state's humans (CGameState +0x60) and the player rows (+0x1320) side by side, stopping when either runs out: a human is made a recipient (row `shield` checkbox unchecked through CCheckBox_UncheckNotify, CHuman +0x29 = 1) where its country is the local player's (idler slot 23), or the local country's CDiplomacyStatus towards it (CCountry +0xE28[id]) has +0x14 not null (an alliance), or the local country's faction (CCountry +0xD8) is valid (slot 7) and is that country's faction too; otherwise it is struck out (checkbox checked, +0x29 = 0). **The row list is never filled, so the walk ends before its first step and the button does nothing.** See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ingamechat.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0x64CCE0..0x64CFAB (bare ret); the loop tests the row at 0x64CDA4 before any work. Stored into the glue at +0x828 (0x647A91), attached to `allies` at 0x65FD2F. That +0x14 of the status is the alliance rests on the record's CDiplomacyStatus fields, not on a new reading.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::OnChatEnemiesButton
addresses.comment: **`chat_window`'s `enemies` button** (glue +0x878; the button's text is CHAT_FOES). Humans and player rows side by side as OnChatAlliesButton: a recipient where the human's country is the state's player (CCurrentGameState +0xC34) or the local country's CDiplomacyStatus towards it has +0x20 not null (a war); struck out otherwise. Dead for the same reason: the rows do not exist.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0x64CFB0..0x64D255 (bare ret); row tested at 0x64D07E. Glue +0x878 (0x647ABB), attached to `enemies` at 0x65FEE3. That status +0x20 is the war is the record's.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::OnChatAllButton
addresses.comment: **`chat_window`'s `all` button** (glue +0x8C8): every player row's `shield` unchecked, then - in a loop of its own, so with or without rows - every human's chat_recipient (CHuman +0x29) = 1.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0x64D260..0x64D37B (bare ret): two separate loops, rows at 0x64D290, humans at 0x64D360. Glue +0x8C8 (0x647AE5), attached to `all` at 0x65FFBD.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::OnChatNoneButton
addresses.comment: **`chat_window`'s `none` button** (glue +0x7D8): humans and player rows side by side, each row's `shield` checked (CCheckBox_CheckNotify) and the human's chat_recipient (+0x29) = 0. With no rows it clears nothing.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0x675200..0x67531F (bare ret); both lists tested at 0x6752A1 and 0x6752A5 before the first step. Glue +0x7D8 (0x647A67), attached to `none` at 0x65FE09.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::OnChatPlayerNameClicked
addresses.comment: A button handler with the pressed button as its argument (glue +0x6C8): the player row whose `name` button it is has its `shield` checkbox toggled - checked (+0x60 = 1) becomes unchecked and the human a recipient (+0x29 = 1), unchecked becomes checked and +0x29 = 0. The elements are those of menubar.gui's `player_entry`; no code makes such a row (the type's name is not in the image), so nothing is attached to this glue.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0x64D380..0x64D5C2 (`ret 4`); `cmp eax, [ebp+8]` at 0x64D470 against the row's `name` (window slot 13). Constructor stores it at 0x64794F for the glue at +0x6C8. 'No code makes a row': the strings `player_entry` and `short_player_entry` do not occur nul-bounded in the image (substring search finds only `multiplayer_entry`, `multiplayer_entry_server`, `ingame_multiplayer_entry`), and no instruction writes or takes the address of +0x1320/+0x1324/+0x1328 but the constructor's zeroes and the destructor's clear.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::OnChatShieldToggled
addresses.comment: The player rows' `shield` checkbox handler (the observer at +0x718, handler stored at +0x728): for every row and human side by side, an unchecked shield hides the row's `minishield_strikeout` icon and sets chat_recipient (+0x29) = 1; a checked one shows the strike-out and clears it. So in the unused design a checked shield is a struck-out player. Never attached: no rows.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0x64D5D0..0x64D7BB (bare ret); `cmp dword ptr [eax+0x60], 1` on the checkbox, icon slot 14 / 13. Stored at 0x64797E into +0x728.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::OnChatMessage
addresses.comment: **A chat line arriving in play: the handler of the CChatMessageObserverGlue<CInGameIdler> at +0x1CE8, told by the screen's chat buffer (+0x1CE4).** (1) Where the message is not to all (+0x24 = 0) and its sender's name (+0x28) is not the local player's, it is shown only where the local player's name is in its recipients (+0x44); otherwise the routine returns. (2) The text (message slot 8) is laid out as CGameSetup::AddChatLine does it - a probe row `chat_entry`, its `text` box's font, a CTextLayout as wide as the box less 10 by 2000 - and split at line breaks. (3) A row a line, added at the end of `chat_list` (+0x1354, list slot 4): the first line in a **`chat_entry`** - `text` the line, `shield` the flag of the message's country (+0x54, icon slot 53), `text_shadow` `§b` + the line + `§W`; every further line in a **`chat_entry_other`** (the two texts, no shield). (4) One message of type **CHATMESSAGE** with TEXT = the whole text, posted to the screen (PostMessage_CInGameIdler). (5) chat_row_timer (+0x1D20) = now, and `chat_list` scrolled. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ingamechat.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0x673690..0x67472C (`ret 4`); the filter at 0x6736C3..0x673870, rows at 0x6738A5 / 0x673BE3 / 0x673FB9, the shadow's two strings at 0x15B66FC (`a7 62`) and 0x15B6700 (`a7 57`), CHATMESSAGE at 0x6744C4. Constructor stores it at 0x648486 beside table 0x15CEDB8, which the RTTI export names CChatMessageObserverGlue<CInGameIdler>. Brief listing for the layout part (calls and strings).

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::OnChatEditEnter
addresses.comment: **Enter in menubar.gui's `chat_message`** (the CTextBufferObserverGlue at +0x1CF8). The text with white space trimmed; nothing where empty. Recipients: for each player row whose `shield` is not checked, that human's name is put on a list; to_all = the list is at least as long as the row list (+0x1328) - **with no rows, 0 >= 0, always to all**. A country chat message (0x74 bytes, table 0x1602474: text, the local player's name, the list, to_all, his country's tag and name) goes into a chat-line command for the screen's chat buffer (+0x1CE4) and is posted through the session; the box is emptied. The window is not closed. **Unreachable in practice**: the box's window is never shown. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ingamechat.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0x674730..0x674E10 (bare ret); `cmp eax, [ecx+0x1328]; jge` at 0x674B0C, ChatAddressedMessage_Construct at 0x674BB4, ChatLineCommand_Construct at 0x674C18, the post through session +0x38 slot 6 at 0x674C44, SetText of the empty string at 0x674D1B. Constructor stores it at 0x6484AB for the glue at +0x1CF8; CInGameIdler_UpdateOpenView attaches the glue to `chat_message` (0x651F0B, 0x652266).

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_ExpireChatRows
addresses.comment: **How long a row of `chat_list` stays.** Every frame, from CInGameIdler::Update (0x655B05). elapsed = (int)(clock seconds - chat_row_timer (+0x1D20)), truncated. With rows in the list: where the row count is above the chat buffer's row limit (+0x1CE4 +0x4C, set to 10 by Enter) **or elapsed > 10**, the first (oldest) row is taken out and deleted and the timer set to now. With no rows the timer is set to now. So a row goes at the earliest 11 seconds after the last line arrived or the last row went, one row at a time, oldest first; there is no fade.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0x674E20..0x674EC3 (bare ret, receiver in EDI): `fsub qword ptr [edi+0x1d20]`, _ftol2_sse, `movzx ebx, word ptr [eax+0x4c]`, `cmp eax, ebx; jg`, `cmp [ebp-4], 0xa; jle`, list slot 8 with (row, 1). One caller, 0x655B05. That list slot 10 is the row count and slot 11 the rows container (count at +8) is read off this use and CGameSetup::AddChatLine's; wrong if slot 10 counts something else.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_UpdateChat
addresses.comment: **The in-play chat's frame, on the game's side**; from CInGameIdler::Update (0x655AE8), every frame. Nothing outside multiplayer (+0x68) or without the chat object (the global at VA 0x1A857E8). In order: BaseChat_Update with the frame's seconds (+0xA8C); once the chat is synced (+0xDC) and has no local user (+0xA4 = -1), a 0x5C-byte command (0xA98DD0: the local CHuman, the session's local human id) is posted and +0xA4 = that id - the local player joins the chat; **every input event of the frame (+0x1CB0) is offered to BaseChat_HandleInput**; on the authority (session +0x34) a 0x40-byte command (0xA99010) is posted for every chat user whose human is no longer in the session; and where the local country's faction (CCountry +0xD8, else the null faction) differs from chat_faction (+0x1DEC), it is remembered and the player is moved to that faction's channel - index 1 `axis`, 2 `allies`, 3 `comintern` by the faction's tag, **4 for no faction or any other** - by a 0x44-byte command (0xA99210: user, channel id), after a 0x48-byte one (0xA99510) where the channel already lists him. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ingamechat.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Brief listing VA 0x6554C0..0x6559CB (`ret 4`): the four tags at 0x6554EA..0x655502 (`axis`, `allies`, `comintern`, and CHAT_NEUTRAL in the fourth place, which no tag equals), the event loop at 0x655680, the channel index `inc esi; imul esi, esi, 0x54`. likely: what the four posted commands do is taken from their arguments and the save-token names (chat_user_joined, chat_user_left, chat_user_joined_channel, chat_user_left_channel), not from their Execute bodies, which were not read; and nothing here takes the player out of his former faction's channel.

addresses.name: BaseChat_UserRowFlagCallback
addresses.signature: void __cdecl BaseChat_UserRowFlagCallback(void* context, void* row, int humanId)
addresses.comment: The callback CInGameIdler::Update gives the chat object (+0x108, with 0 at +0x10C) when it makes it: for the human of that id (CHuman +0x1C) the row's `country_icon` button (chat.gui's `user_item`) is given the human's country (button slot 53, the tag's id) - the flag beside a name in the chat's `users` list. Nothing for an unknown id.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0x655380..0x6554B9 (bare rets); `cmp [esi+0x1c], ecx` with ecx = [ebp+0x10], window slot 13 on [ebp+0xc] with `country_icon`. Stored at 0x6563C4. likely: the convention is read off the frame (arguments at +0xC and +0x10, bare ret); its caller inside the chat was not read, so the first argument is unknown.

addresses.name: CClientPingCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: Slot 6 of CClientPingCommand: a client's report of its date. The human of the command's id (+0x40) gets mp_tick (CHuman +0x4C) = the command's tick (+0x3C); the rest only on the authority (session +0x34). behind = the state's day less the client's day. **behind > 10**: the first time only the day is remembered (0x1BEBD20, flag bit 1 of 0x1BEBD24); on a later day the screen's slot 27 (TogglePause) and a chat line **LAG_PAUSE** ("$PLAYER$ is lagging behind, pausing game."). **Otherwise behind > 5**: the same with 0x1BEBD1C and bit 2, the screen's slot 26 (DecreaseSpeed) and **LAG_DECREASE_SPEED**. PLAYER is the lagging human's name + ` (@` + his country's tag + `)`. The line is a country chat message from the authority's own player (his name, his country), to all, in a chat-line command for the chat buffer found by the fixed id pair at 0x17103FC - so every screen shows it in `chat_list` and raises CHATMESSAGE. At most one line a game day for each of the two. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ingamechat.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0x6DAA30..0x6DB2D1 (bare rets); vtable.py --holding: CClientPingCommand slot 6 (table 0x15D36AC). `cmp eax, 0xa; jle` at 0x6DABD8, `cmp eax, 5; jle` at 0x6DAF35, slots 0x6C and 0x68 on the screen, LAG_PAUSE at 0x6DAD81, LAG_DECREASE_SPEED at 0x6DB0DE, `push 1` for to_all. likely: that the two date sums are days (hours / 24 folded with a 365-day year) was read in outline, not worked through; the slots' names are the record's.

addresses.name: CMultiplayerHandler::OnSessionInfo
addresses.comment: Slot 1 of CMultiplayerHandler: the session's events while a game is played. **Read only for event 5 (players lost), and that in a brief listing**: the handler's window `player_lost_window` (+8) is filled - `Title` PLAYER_LOST_TITLE, `Description` PLAYER_LOST_DESC with `playername` the lost players' names joined - a CAddPlayer(remove) is posted for each, the window shown, and where the game is not paused (screen slot 95) a 0x5C-byte command (0x6D7F10, with the local player) is posted; then **a country chat line from the local player, to all, whose text is the rendered description** (likely - the same text object is rendered again), in a chat-line command for the chat buffer of the fixed id pair at 0x17103FC. The other strings of the body - SERVER_LOST_TITLE / SERVER_LOST_DESC, INITIAL_HOTJOIN_REQUEST / HOTJOIN_TITLE in a `DefaultDialog` - belong to events not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ingamechat.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: vtable.py --holding 0x645900: CMultiplayerHandler slot 1 (table 0x15CED28, offset 0). `cmp eax, 5; jne 0x6467a0` at 0x645933; exits `ret 4` (0x645E80, 0x64679D, 0x6469E1, 0x646D8B, 0x646E3A). ChatAddressedMessage_Construct at 0x646553 with `push 1`, table 0x1602474 written at 0x646573, ChatLineCommand_Construct at 0x6465E9. Wrong about the text if the object rendered at 0x6464E6 is not the one rendered into `Description` at 0x646093.

addresses.name: BaseChat_Create
addresses.signature: void* __cdecl BaseChat_Create(void* session, void* arg2, void* gui, void* arg4, const char** channelNames)
addresses.comment: Makes the in-play chat object, a 0x120-byte object with no RTTI name (table VA 0x15FF524, 6 slots; `BaseChat` is ours, after its tooltip group BASECHAT), and stores it in the global at VA 0x1A857E8, deleting an earlier one (slot 1) first. One caller: CInGameIdler::Update (0x6563BA), in multiplayer only (+0x68) and only while the global is null, with the screen's slots 18, 16, 14 and 17 and the four localised names CHAT_AXIS, CHAT_ALLIES, CHAT_COMINTERN, CHAT_NEUTRAL; Update then stores BaseChat_UserRowFlagCallback at +0x108, **hides `chat_window` (window slot 9) and shows `chat_inbox_window` (slot 8)**, and posts a 0x3C-byte command (0xA9A480; likely the request for the chat's state, token name chat_request_sync). ProcessSessionEndRequests deletes the object (0x654342, 0x654580, 0x6547DF).
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0xA94D20..0xA94DB4 (bare rets, five stack arguments passed on to BaseChat_Construct); `push 0x120` before operator new; the caller's block at 0x65627D..0x65644A tests `cmp byte ptr [ebx+0x68], 0` and `cmp dword ptr [0x1a857e8], esi`. inferred within it: which screen slot is the session and which the gui (slot 18's result is used as the session elsewhere, slot 14 is the record's gui); the posted command's meaning.

addresses.name: BaseChat_Construct
addresses.signature: void* __stdcall BaseChat_Construct(void* this, void* session, void* arg2, void* gui, void* arg4, const char** channelNames)
addresses.comment: The chat object's constructor. Registers itself as a reloadable interface piece under the gui type name `chat_window` (base table 0x15FDB48); keeps its four pointers at +0x20..+0x2C; three glues - the input box's at +0x38 (table 0x15FF704), `close`'s at +0x4C and `open`'s at +0x78 (handlers BaseChat_Close and BaseChat_Open); local user +0xA4 = -1; **eleven slash commands** in the vector at +0xA8 (0x44 bytes each): `/slap`, `/me`, `/whisper`, `/reply`, `/invite`, `/create`, `/ban`, `/kick`, `/roll`, `/?`, `/help`; **five channels** (0xA94AB0): CHAT_CHANNEL_GENERAL localised, then the four names given (+0x118 = 4); then BaseChat_Build.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0xA92780..0xA92F0D (`ret 0x18`); the eleven strings at 0x15FEFB8..0x15FF004 (0x15FF000 is `/?`), `mov dword ptr [esi+0x118], 4`, the loop over [ebp+0x1c] calling 0xA94AB0. Not read: 0xA94AB0 and what the two flags it is given mean.

addresses.name: BaseChat_Build
addresses.comment: Slot 0 of the chat's table: makes its two windows from **interface/chat.gui** - `chat_window` (+0x30; an old one deleted first) and `chat_inbox_window` (+0x34) - through the gui factory at VA 0x1A857D8. `chat_window`'s edit box **`chat_input`** gets the glue at +0x38 (Enter), its button **`close`** BaseChat_Close; `chat_inbox_window`'s button **`open`** BaseChat_Open; both windows are put in the tooltip group **BASECHAT** and shown; then, as built, the chat window is shown and the inbox hidden (CInGameIdler::Update reverses that at once after making the object), alert (+0x106) = 0, the current channel's unread mark cleared, and the three lists filled: `channels` (0xA937F0), `users` (0xA93A10), `chat` (BaseChat_RebuildList). Returns true.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0xA93300..0xA935E9 (bare ret, `mov al, 1`); the strings `chat_window`, `chat_input`, `close`, `BASECHAT`, `chat_inbox_window`, `open` in that order. Window slot 8 is show (writes +0x5B = 1, VA 0xAC2650) and slot 9 hide (0xAC2230).

addresses.name: BaseChat_Open
addresses.comment: **Opens the in-play chat**: alert (+0x106) = 0, `chat_window` shown (window slot 8), `chat_inbox_window` hidden (slot 9), the current channel's unread mark (+0x50) cleared, and `channels`, `users` and `chat` filled again. The handler of the inbox window's `open` button; BaseChat_HandleInput calls it for Tab while the window is hidden.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0xA932A0..0xA932DF (bare ret). Stored into the glue at +0x78 (0xA9287F), attached to `open` in BaseChat_Build (0xA93522); called at 0xA95219.

addresses.name: BaseChat_Close
addresses.no_signature: ECX is the chat; no stack arguments; it ends in a tail jump through the inbox window's slot 8, so it has no ret of its own
addresses.comment: **Closes the in-play chat**: `chat_window` hidden (window slot 9) and `chat_inbox_window` shown (slot 8). The handler of `chat_window`'s `close` button, whose shortcut in chat.gui is TAB. Nothing else: the input box keeps its text and the keyboard.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0xA932E0..0xA932F6 (`jmp edx`). Stored into the glue at +0x4C (0xA92854), attached to `close` in BaseChat_Build (0xA93411).

addresses.name: BaseChat_Update
addresses.no_signature: register convention: the chat in ESI and the frame's seconds in XMM0; bare ret
addresses.comment: The chat's frame, from CInGameIdler_UpdateChat. Adds the frame's seconds to the blink timer (+0x11C), kept below 1.0. While the inbox window is shown (the chat is closed) it sets the frame of the `open` button (button slot 18): **with the alert (+0x106) set, frame 1 while the timer is under 0.5 and frame 2 otherwise** - a blink with a period of a second; without it, **frame 2 where a channel the local user is in has an unread mark** (0xA93220) and frame 1 otherwise.
addresses.evidence: Brief listing VA 0xA935F0..0xA937E4: the compare with the single at 0x15AB304 and the pushes of 1 and 2 before slot 0x48 of the `open` button. likely: 0.5 for the constant at 0x15AB304 and 1.0 for the wrap were not read off the bytes; who sets +0x106 was not looked for.

addresses.name: BaseChat_HandleInput
addresses.comment: **The in-play chat's keys**, given each input event of the frame by CInGameIdler_UpdateChat (the event's layout is CInGameIdler +0x1CB0's). **Window hidden**: a key event with code 9, **Tab, opens the chat** (BaseChat_Open) and is marked handled; nothing else. **Window shown** (and the chat synced, +0xDC, and `chat_input` found): **Escape (0x1B) closes** - window hidden, inbox shown; **Up (0x26, key down)** and the down key step the history index (+0xFC) and recall a sent line (0xA959A0); a key with the input empty and a last whisperer known (+0x100, still a user) puts **`/reply `** in the box once (+0x104); **Tab** - with Ctrl held (the gui keyboard's slot 12; Shift, slot 10, the other way) the next channel the local user is in becomes current (0xA94C90), otherwise the last word of the input is completed: a lone word starting `/` to a slash command, any other to a user's name and a space. Each of these marks the event handled.
addresses.evidence: Brief listing VA 0xA951D0..0xA9598E (`ret 8` at seven exits): `cmp dword ptr [esi], 9` at 0xA9520E and 0xA954A9, `cmp ecx, 0x1b` at 0xA952BC, `cmp ecx, 0x26` at 0xA952F5, `/reply ` at 0xA95403, `cmp byte ptr [eax], 0x2f` at 0xA9567E. likely: which key prefills `/reply ` (the test on [ebp+0xb] was not traced back), and the Backspace arm at 0xA95356, were not settled; whether this runs before or after the interface's own input pass was not established.

addresses.name: BaseChat_OnInputEnter
addresses.no_signature: slot 2 of the chat's own table (VA 0x15FF524, no RTTI); the chat arrives in ECX (inferred - the body uses it from EDI), no stack arguments, bare ret
addresses.comment: **Enter in `chat_input`.** The text trimmed of white space; **nothing where it is empty**. A line starting `/` goes to the slash-command dispatch (0xA950F0); where that refuses it, the system line CHAT_ERROR_UNKNOWNSLASH is written into the current channel on this machine alone. Any other line is posted as a 0x6C-byte command (0xA988B0: the local user's id +0xA4, the current channel's id +0xD8, the text, 0, 1) through the session - a line for the current channel. Then **the box is emptied**, the line is kept in the input history (+0xE4), the history index (+0xFC) = -1 and +0x104 = 0. The window stays open.
addresses.evidence: Brief listing VA 0xA942B0..0xA944C3: TrimWhitespace, `cmp byte ptr [ecx], 0x2f`, CHAT_ERROR_UNKNOWNSLASH at 0xA943AD, `push 0x6c` and the post through [chat+0x20]+0x38 slot 6 at 0xA94434, SetText of the empty string. likely: the command's Execute (how the line reaches the other machines' channel) was not read; the glue's stored handler is 0x698C90, taken to be a thunk to this slot.

addresses.name: BaseChat_AddSystemLine
addresses.no_signature: register convention not decoded: three stack arguments (ret 0xC) and a channel record in a register
addresses.comment: Writes a line into a channel's own list of lines (+0x38 of the 0x54-byte channel record) and, where that channel is the current one, fills the `chat` list again. With the time flag set the line opens with the local clock as **`[%H:%M]`**; a line with no user (-1) is signed with CHAT_SYSTEM ("System") and `: `, another with the user's name. Then the unread mark: cleared where the channel is current and the window shown, set otherwise - and `channels` drawn again where it changed.
addresses.evidence: Brief listing VA 0xA971A0..0xA97369 (`ret 0xc`): the format string at 0x15FF268, CHAT_SYSTEM at 0xA97265, the compare of [chat+0xD8] with the channel's id (+0x34) and of the window's +0x5B. likely: the order of the line's parts was not put together from the appends.

addresses.name: BaseChat_AddLine
addresses.no_signature: register convention not decoded: four stack arguments (ret 0x10) and a channel record in a register
addresses.comment: A user's line into a channel, as BaseChat_AddSystemLine: signed CHAT_SYSTEM for no user, **CHAT_WHISPER_TO ("To $NAME$") where the sender is the local user**, the sender's name otherwise; with the local clock as `[%H:%M]: `. Kept in the channel's lines and the `chat` list filled again.
addresses.evidence: Brief listing VA 0xA97370..0xA974F9 (`ret 0x10`): `cmp edi, [edx+0xa4]`, CHAT_WHISPER_TO at 0xA97431, the format string at 0x15FF28C. likely: the order of name and time, and the flag that chooses the whisper form, were not settled.

addresses.name: BaseChat_RebuildList
addresses.no_signature: register convention not decoded: the channel (or null for the current one) in ECX and the chat on the stack (ret 4)
addresses.comment: Fills chat.gui's `chat` list box from the current channel's lines: nothing where the channel given is not the current one; a probe row `chat_item` gives its `text` box's font and width, each kept line is laid out to that width and split at line breaks, and every piece becomes a row `chat_item` (0xA97DC0) with its `text` set; the list is then scrolled (slots 24, 30, 27).
addresses.evidence: Brief listing VA 0xA93B90..0xA9417B (`ret 4`): `chat_item` at 0xA93BDA, `text` at 0xA93C3B, `chat` at 0xA93D00, String_Split with 0xA, the row object of 0x48 bytes. likely: read for its strings and calls only; the two further `ret 0x18` at 0xA9421A and 0xA9429F belong to the functions after it.

addresses.name: ChatAddressedMessage_Construct
addresses.signature: void* __stdcall ChatAddressedMessage_Construct(void* this, Hoi3CString* text, Hoi3CString* sender, void* recipients, bool toAll)
addresses.comment: The constructor of the chat message with recipients (0x54 bytes, table VA 0x1602450, persistent type 0x12E, no RTTI name): text at +8, **to_all at +0x24**, the sender's name at +0x28, and at +0x44 a list of the recipients' names copied from the list given. The country chat message (table 0x1602474, type 0x152, token name `countrychat`, 0x74 bytes) is this with the sender's country tag at +0x54 and country name at +0x58; CInGameIdler::OnChatEditEnter and CMultiplayerHandler::OnSessionInfo write that table over this one's by hand, and ChatCountryMessage_Construct does it for CClientPingCommand::Execute.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0xAC9A20..0xAC9AD0 (`ret 0x14`): `mov byte ptr [esi+0x24], cl` from [ebp+0x18], the list loop into +0x44. Callers 0x646553, 0x674BB4, 0xACA287. Table 0x1602450 slot 6 answers 0x12E, 0x1602474 slot 6 answers 0x152.

addresses.name: ChatCountryMessage_Construct
addresses.no_signature: register convention: five stack arguments (ret 0x14) with two more in ECX and EDX, which it pushes on to ChatAddressedMessage_Construct
addresses.comment: Builds a country chat message (table VA 0x1602474): ChatAddressedMessage_Construct, then the country's tag id at +0x54 and its name at +0x58. Called by CClientPingCommand::Execute for the two lag lines.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0xACA260..0xACA2C8 (`ret 0x14`); `mov dword ptr [esi], 0x1602474`. Callers 0x6DADFD, 0x6DB15A.

addresses.name: ChatCountryMessage_GetText
addresses.no_signature: a virtual of a class the RTTI export does not name; ECX is the message, one stack argument (the string to fill), ret 4
addresses.comment: Slot 8 of the country chat message's table (VA 0x1602474): **the line as `chat_list` and CHATMESSAGE show it.** With a country name (+0x58): **sender + ` (` + country + `)` + `: ` + text** where the message is to all, and **`*: ` in place of `: ` where it is not** - the mark of a line for chosen recipients. With no country name it answers as the table below it does (ChatAddressedMessage_GetText). No colour code is added, unlike the lobby's player line.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0xACA520..0xACAA4F (`ret 4`): the flag at 0xACA580 (name not empty and +0x24 = 0), the strings ` (` (0x15BDBE4), `)` (0x15B6C98), `*: ` (0x16023E0) on the first arm and `: ` (0x15B6B80) on the second, the fall to 0xAC9FC0.

addresses.name: ChatAddressedMessage_GetText
addresses.no_signature: a virtual of a class the RTTI export does not name; ECX is the message, one stack argument (the string to fill), ret 4
addresses.comment: Slot 8 of the addressed chat message's table (VA 0x1602450): sender + `> ` + text where the message is not to all, sender + `*> ` + text where it is, and the text alone with no sender. Note the star is the other way round from ChatCountryMessage_GetText's.
addresses.evidence: Listing VA 0xAC9FC0..0xACA252 (`ret 4`): the flag at 0xACA01E (sender not empty and +0x24 = 0) chooses `> ` (0x16023D8, two bytes); the second arm `*> ` (0x16023DC, three bytes).

structs.name: BaseChat
structs.comment: The in-play multiplayer chat object (0x120 bytes by its one `operator new`, table VA 0x15FF524 with 6 slots, no RTTI name - the name is ours, after its tooltip group BASECHAT). One at a time, in the global at VA 0x1A857E8; made by CInGameIdler::Update in multiplayer through BaseChat_Create, built from interface/chat.gui. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ingamechat.md. `size` is left out: only the allocation was read.
structs.evidence: `push 0x120; call operator new` in BaseChat_Create (0xA94D58); `mov dword ptr [esi], 0x15ff524` in BaseChat_Construct (0xA92826). Not in the RTTI export (no class holds a table at 0x15FF524).

struct_fields.name: chat_recipient
struct_fields.comment: Whether this player is a recipient of the next line typed in menubar.gui's `chat_window`: written by the four recipient buttons' handlers and the two player-row handlers of CInGameIdler. **No reader was found** - CInGameIdler::OnChatEditEnter builds its recipient list from the rows' checkboxes, not from this - and of its writers only OnChatAllButton can run without player rows, which never exist. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ingamechat.md, section 2.
struct_fields.evidence: Stores `mov byte ptr [reg+0x29], 0/1` at 0x64CF1B, 0x64CF88, 0x64D1CB, 0x64D22D, 0x64D360, 0x64D53A, 0x64D595, 0x64D735, 0x64D78E, 0x675302, each with reg walking CGameState +0x60 by +0x54. 'No reader' is from those six functions and OnChatEditEnter only - no image-wide scan of +0x29 was made (the displacement is too common to scan bare).

struct_fields.name: chat_player_name_observer
struct_fields.comment: A button observer glue whose handler is CInGameIdler::OnChatPlayerNameClicked; meant for the `name` button of a chat player row. Never attached.

struct_fields.name: chat_shield_observer
struct_fields.comment: An observer (handler at +0x728) for a chat player row's `shield` checkbox: CInGameIdler::OnChatShieldToggled. Never attached.

struct_fields.name: chat_close_observer
struct_fields.comment: CButtonObserverGlue: CInGameIdler::CloseChatWindow, on `chat_window`'s `closebutton`.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x647A3D (`lea eax, [ebx+0x788]`); Enter 0x65FC4E attaches it to `closebutton` of `chat_window`.

struct_fields.name: chat_none_observer
struct_fields.comment: CButtonObserverGlue: CInGameIdler::OnChatNoneButton, on `chat_window`'s `none`.

struct_fields.name: chat_allies_observer
struct_fields.comment: CButtonObserverGlue: CInGameIdler::OnChatAlliesButton, on `chat_window`'s `allies`.

struct_fields.name: chat_enemies_observer
struct_fields.comment: CButtonObserverGlue: CInGameIdler::OnChatEnemiesButton, on `chat_window`'s `enemies`.

struct_fields.name: chat_all_observer
struct_fields.comment: CButtonObserverGlue: CInGameIdler::OnChatAllButton, on `chat_window`'s `all`.

struct_fields.name: message_log_toggle_observer
struct_fields.comment: CButtonObserverGlue: CInGameIdler::ToggleMessageLog, on `messagelog_window`'s `closebutton` and the menubar's `OPENbutton`.

struct_fields.name: chat_player_rows
struct_fields.comment: Head of a list (tail +0x1324, count +0x1328) of chat player rows - nodes of a name string, the row's window at +0x1C and the next node at +0x24 - that the recipient handlers and CInGameIdler::OnChatEditEnter walk beside the state's humans. **Never filled**: the image holds no instruction that adds to it, so it is always empty.
struct_fields.evidence: Every instruction with a 0x1320 displacement or immediate in .text (byte search for the four bytes, each hit decoded in place): the constructor's zero (0x6480B5), the destructor's clear (0x6499BA, 0x679A80), and seven reads (0x64CD8C, 0x64D056, 0x64D27D, 0x64D41B, 0x64D66B, 0x6749F0, 0x675298). +0x1324: the constructor's zero only. +0x1328: the constructor's zero and the compare at 0x674B0C. Positive control: the same search finds the seven readers. Wrong if a row is appended through a pointer computed some other way.

struct_fields.name: ingame_lobby
struct_fields.comment: The CIngameLobby (0x1A0 bytes, 0x6915D0), made by Enter in multiplayer only with the session's configuration (+0x968) and the screen's chat buffer (+0x1CE4); deleted by Leave. Until it reports itself done (its +0xF5) the screen does not listen to the chat buffer (CInGameIdler_UpdateOpenView).
struct_fields.evidence: Enter 0x660696..0x6606DD (`cmp byte ptr [ebx+0x68], 0`; `push 0x1a0`; result stored at +0x1CD0); Leave 0x662169; UpdateOpenView 0x651E35..0x651E69.

struct_fields.name: chat_buffer
struct_fields.comment: The screen's chat buffer (0xACAC30, as the lobby's CGameSetup +0x3BC), made by Enter in single player and multiplayer alike with a **row limit (+0x4C) of 10**; deleted by Leave. Chat-line commands hand it their message and it tells its observers - the in-game lobby, and the screen's CInGameIdler::OnChatMessage.
struct_fields.evidence: Enter 0x65D63C..0x65D6A3: the result stored at +0x1CE4 and `mov word ptr [eax+0x4c], dx` with edx = 0xA. Leave 0x66217B.

struct_fields.name: chat_observer
struct_fields.comment: A CChatMessageObserverGlue<CInGameIdler> (table 0x15CEDB8), handler CInGameIdler::OnChatMessage; registered with the chat buffer's observers (+0x30 of the buffer) once, by CInGameIdler_UpdateOpenView.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x648486..0x6484A1; UpdateOpenView 0x651E6F..0x651E7F and 0x6521D0..0x6521E0 (0x6792C0 with the buffer + 0x30 and this glue).

struct_fields.name: chat_edit_observer
struct_fields.comment: A CTextBufferObserverGlue (table 0x15CEDC4), handler CInGameIdler::OnChatEditEnter; attached to `chat_window`'s `chat_message` once, by CInGameIdler_UpdateOpenView. ReloadMenubar makes the box again and does not attach it again.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x6484AB..0x6484E0; UpdateOpenView 0x651F04 and 0x65225F (the box's layout +0x48 slot 1 with this glue).

struct_fields.name: chat_observers_attached
struct_fields.comment: Set once the two chat glues (+0x1CE8, +0x1CF8) are attached: by the first frame's CInGameIdler_UpdateOpenView where there is no in-game lobby, or once the lobby's +0xF5 is set.
struct_fields.evidence: UpdateOpenView: `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x1d18], bl` at 0x651E63 and 0x6521C4, `mov byte ptr [edi+0x1d18], 1` at 0x651E8F and 0x6521F0.

struct_fields.name: chat_row_timer
struct_fields.comment: The clock's seconds when a chat line last arrived or a `chat_list` row was last taken away; CInGameIdler_ExpireChatRows takes the oldest row away once more than 10 whole seconds have passed since.
struct_fields.evidence: `fstp qword ptr [reg+0x1d20]` at 0x65D4F1 (Enter), 0x674668 (OnChatMessage), 0x674EB8; `fsub qword ptr [edi+0x1d20]` at 0x674E39.

struct_fields.name: message_log_open
struct_fields.comment: Whether the message log window is open, as CInGameIdler::ToggleMessageLog left it; CInGameIdler::CloseChatWindow toggles the log where it is set.
struct_fields.evidence: All four accesses in the image: the constructor's zero (0x64856E), ToggleMessageLog's stores (0x64CA61, 0x64CA6C), CloseChatWindow's test (0x64CBC1).

struct_fields.name: chat_faction
struct_fields.comment: The faction whose chat channel the local player was last put in; CInGameIdler_UpdateChat compares it with the local country's faction each frame.
struct_fields.evidence: CInGameIdler_UpdateChat: `cmp dword ptr [ebx+0x1dec], esi` at 0x65582B and the store at 0x655849. No other access was looked for.

struct_fields.name: session
struct_fields.comment: The first of the four pointers the chat is made with; commands are posted through its +0x38 (slot 6), so it is the session.

struct_fields.name: window
struct_fields.comment: chat.gui's `chat_window`.

struct_fields.name: inbox_window
struct_fields.comment: chat.gui's `chat_inbox_window`, the icon shown while the chat is closed; its `open` button opens the chat.

struct_fields.name: local_user_id
struct_fields.comment: The local player's human id once he has joined the chat; -1 before.
struct_fields.evidence: BaseChat_Construct 0xA928B9 (-1); CInGameIdler_UpdateChat 0x655552 (test) and 0x65566A (store of the session's +0x6C).

struct_fields.name: slash_commands
struct_fields.comment: Vector (end +0xAC) of the eleven slash commands, 0x44 bytes each, the name first.

struct_fields.name: users
struct_fields.comment: Vector (end +0xBC) of the chat's users, 0x20 bytes each, the human id first.

struct_fields.name: channels
struct_fields.comment: Vector (end +0xCC) of channel records, 0x54 bytes each: members (ids) at +0x20/+0x24, the channel's id at +0x34, its lines at +0x38, an unread mark at +0x50. Index 0 is General, 1 to 4 the four faction channels.

struct_fields.name: current_channel_id
struct_fields.comment: The id of the channel shown and written to.

struct_fields.name: synced
struct_fields.comment: Set once the chat has its state; until then the local player does not join and the open window takes no keys. inferred: its writer was not read.
struct_fields.evidence: Tests at 0x655545, 0x65583C (CInGameIdler_UpdateChat) and 0xA9523C (BaseChat_HandleInput); zeroed by the constructor (0xA92903).

struct_fields.name: history_index
struct_fields.comment: Which sent line Up and Down have recalled; -1 for none.

struct_fields.name: alert
struct_fields.comment: While set and the chat is closed, the inbox's `open` button blinks; cleared by opening the chat. inferred: its setter was not read.

struct_fields.name: user_row_callback
struct_fields.comment: A function the game gives the chat for decorating a user's row: BaseChat_UserRowFlagCallback (with 0 at +0x10C).

struct_fields.name: blink_timer
struct_fields.comment: Seconds, wrapped: the phase of the inbox button's blink.

slots_noted: The chat object's own table (VA 0x15FF524, 6 slots: 0 BaseChat_Build, 1 the deleting destructor 0xA92F40, 2 BaseChat_OnInputEnter, 3 0xA97EE0, 4 0x414A20, 5 0x414A80) and the four chat message tables (0x16023E4 base, 0x1602408 system, 0x160242C player, 0x1602450 addressed, 0x1602474 country; slot 6 the persistent type, slot 8 GetText) have no RTTI class, so no vftable_slots record can carry them. CChatBuffer::CWriteToChatBuffer (table 0x15E3FE4, type 0x149, Execute 0xACAF40) is a second chat command beside the record's ChatLineCommand (table 0x16024F4, type 0x14B, token name `chatmessage`); it was not read and no caller of its Execute was found.
